validated_results.title: [Relationship between dietary nutrients intakes and human prostate cancer].
validated_results.journal: Wei sheng yan jiu = Journal of hygiene research
validated_results.reason: Matched case-control study in humans reporting a multivariable-adjusted odds ratio for dietary retinol (vitamin A) intake and histologically confirmed incident prostate cancer.

extraction.timing: retrospective dietary assessment based on mean food intakes in the latest 3 days
extraction.population: Men with histologically confirmed prostate cancer and healthy matched controls

sample_size.excerpt: In order to study the relationship between dietary nutrients intakes and prostate cancer, 1 : 1 matched case-control study was carried out with 102 patients suffered from histologically confirmed prostate cancer and 102 healthy controls.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 102 + 102 = 204

cases.excerpt: In order to study the relationship between dietary nutrients intakes and prostate cancer, 1 : 1 matched case-control study was carried out with 102 patients suffered from histologically confirmed prostate cancer and 102 healthy controls.

effect_size.excerpt: The multivariable adjusted ORs were 1.65 (95% confident interval (CI) 1.39-1.96) for lipid, 1.22 (95% CI 1.13-1.31) for carbohydrates, 3.21 (95% CI 2.18-4.75) for retinol, 0.61 (95% CI 0.6-0.80) for vitamin C, and 0.029 (95% CI 0.009-0.09) for vitamin B1. The authors discussed the possible mechanism of dietary nutrients contributing to the risk of prostate cancer.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The multivariable adjusted ORs were 1.65 (95% confident interval (CI) 1.39-1.96) for lipid, 1.22 (95% CI 1.13-1.31) for carbohydrates, 3.21 (95% CI 2.18-4.75) for retinol, 0.61 (95% CI 0.6-0.80) for vitamin C, and 0.029 (95% CI 0.009-0.09) for vitamin B1.
